# Sirach Chapter 6 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Sirach 6 (37 verses)
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 22

---

## Disagreement 001 — v.2: "your own soul's counsel" vs. "your own counsel"

**EMET:** "Do not exalt yourself by your own soul's counsel"
**LOGOS:** "Do not put your confidence in your own counsel"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't trust your own judgment so much that it tears you to pieces"
**Issue:** Greek en tē ischyi tēs psychēs sou = "in the strength of your soul." LOGOS drops "soul." PNEUMA adds "so much." Consensus: "Do not exalt yourself by your own counsel."

---

## Disagreement 002 — v.3: "dry tree" vs. "withered tree"

**EMET:** "you will be left like a dry tree"
**LOGOS:** "you will be left like a withered tree"
**PNEUMA:** "you will stand there like a dead tree"
**Issue:** Greek xylon xeron = "dry/withered wood/tree." Both "dry" and "withered" are accurate. Consensus: "a dried-up tree."

---

## Disagreement 003 — v.4: "laughingstock" vs. "mockery"

**EMET:** "makes it the laughingstock of its enemies"
**LOGOS:** "makes it a mockery to its enemies"
**PNEUMA:** "turns them into a joke for their enemies"
**Issue:** Greek katagelōta = "laughingstock/object of ridicule." Both "laughingstock" and "mockery" are accurate. Consensus: "a mockery to its enemies."

---

## Disagreement 004 — v.5: "multiplies friends" vs. "wins many friends"

**EMET:** "A pleasant word multiplies friends"
**LOGOS:** "A pleasant manner wins many friends"
**PNEUMA:** "A pleasant manner makes you a lot of friends"
**Issue:** EMET "word" vs. LOGOS/PNEUMA "manner." Greek stoma = "mouth/speech." EMET is closer to literal ("pleasant speech"). Consensus: "Pleasant speech multiplies friends."

---

## Disagreement 005 — v.6: "let your advisors be one in a thousand" vs. "let your counselors be one in a thousand"

**EMET:** "let your advisors be one in a thousand"
**LOGOS:** "let your counselors be one in a thousand"
**PNEUMA:** "your real counselors should be few; one in a thousand is enough"
**Issue:** Minor word choice. Greek symbouloi = "counselors." PNEUMA expands. Consensus: LOGOS.

---

## Disagreement 006 — v.8: "only for a season" vs. "only for his own convenience"

**EMET:** "there is a friend who is such only for a season"
**LOGOS:** "some are friends only for their own convenience"
**PNEUMA:** "some people are your friend only when times are good"
**Issue:** Greek eis kairon = "for a time/season." EMET is literal; LOGOS interprets it as self-interest (which is the implied meaning). Consensus: "a friend who is such only for a season."

---

## Disagreement 007 — v.9: "disclose a quarrel" vs. "expose your quarrel"

**EMET:** "he will disclose a quarrel to your shame"
**LOGOS:** "will expose your quarrel to your disgrace"
**PNEUMA:** "will turn around and expose your private conflicts to embarrass you"
**Issue:** Greek anakalyypsei neikos = "will uncover/reveal a dispute." Both "disclose" and "expose" are accurate. Consensus: "will expose your quarrel to your disgrace."

---

## Disagreement 008 — v.10: "table-companion" vs. "companion at the table"

**EMET:** "a friend who is a table-companion"
**LOGOS:** "companions at the table"
**PNEUMA:** "companions are great at the dinner table"
**Issue:** Greek hetairos tēs trapezēs = "companion of the table." EMET hyphenates it as a compound; LOGOS separates. Consensus: "a companion at the table."

---

## Disagreement 009 — v.11: "freely commands your servants" vs. "make free with your servants"

**EMET:** "he freely commands your servants"
**LOGOS:** "make free with your servants"
**PNEUMA:** "feel at home with your household"
**Issue:** Greek exousiasai en tois oiketiais sou = "will have authority over your servants/household." LOGOS "make free with" is idiomatic. Consensus: LOGOS.

---

## Disagreement 010 — v.14: "sturdy shelter" vs. "secure fortress"

**EMET:** "A faithful friend is a sturdy shelter"
**LOGOS:** "A faithful friend is a secure fortress"
**PNEUMA:** "A faithful friend is like a strong fortress"
**Issue:** Greek skepē krataia = "strong covering/shelter." LOGOS/PNEUMA "fortress" interprets. EMET "shelter" is more literal. Consensus: "a sturdy shelter."

---

## Disagreement 011 — v.16: "life-saving medicine" vs. "life-giving medicine"

**EMET:** "A faithful friend is a life-saving medicine"
**LOGOS:** "A faithful friend is a life-giving medicine"
**PNEUMA:** "A faithful friend is medicine that keeps you alive"
**Issue:** Greek pharmakon zōēs = "medicine of life." "Life-saving" (EMET) and "life-giving" (LOGOS) both work. Consensus: "a life-saving medicine."

---

## Disagreement 012 — v.17: "makes true friendships" vs. "cultivates true friendship"

**EMET:** "whoever fears the Lord makes true friendships"
**LOGOS:** "one who fears the Lord cultivates true friendship"
**PNEUMA:** "people who fear the Lord build real friendships"
**Issue:** Greek katorthoi tēn philian autou = "sets aright/makes right his friendship." "Makes true" (EMET) is literal. Consensus: EMET.

---

## Disagreement 013 — v.18: "until you are old" vs. "until your hair is white"

**EMET:** "until you are old you will keep finding wisdom"
**LOGOS:** "until your hair is white you will keep finding wisdom"
**PNEUMA:** "you will still be finding wisdom when your hair is white"
**Issue:** Greek heōs presbytes = "until you are old." "Until your hair is white" is interpretive but vivid. Consensus: "until you are old you will keep finding wisdom."

---

## Disagreement 014 — v.20: "how very harsh" vs. "how harsh she seems"

**EMET:** "How very harsh she is to the undisciplined"
**LOGOS:** "How harsh she seems to the undisciplined"
**PNEUMA:** "To undisciplined people, wisdom seems impossibly harsh"
**Issue:** Greek tracheia esti = "she is rough/harsh." EMET "is harsh" is objective; LOGOS "seems harsh" is phenomenological. Both perspectives are valid. Consensus: "How harsh she is to the undisciplined."

---

## Disagreement 015 — v.21: "stone of testing" vs. "testing stone"

**EMET:** "like a heavy stone of testing"
**LOGOS:** "like a stone of testing"
**PNEUMA:** "like a heavy testing stone"
**Issue:** Greek lithō peirasou = "a stone of trial/testing." All say "testing stone" in different word orders. Consensus: "a heavy stone of testing."

---

## Disagreement 016 — v.22: "discipline is like her name" vs. "wisdom lives up to her name"

**EMET:** "discipline is like her name"
**LOGOS:** "wisdom lives up to her name"
**PNEUMA:** "Wisdom earns her name"
**Issue:** Greek paideia = "instruction/discipline." EMET uses the Greek word's meaning ("discipline is like her name"). LOGOS explains why. The wordplay on paideia is untranslatable. Consensus: "For wisdom is true to her name."

---

## Disagreement 017 — v.24: "fetters" vs. "chains"

**EMET:** "Put your feet into her fetters"
**LOGOS:** "Put your feet into her fetters"
**PNEUMA:** "Put your feet in her chains"
**Issue:** Greek pedē = "fetters/shackles." EMET and LOGOS agree. PNEUMA uses "chains." Consensus: "fetters" — the specific instrument (ankle restraints) is more evocative.

---

## Disagreement 018 — v.25: "do not be weary of her bonds" vs. "do not chafe under her bonds"

**EMET:** "do not be weary of her bonds"
**LOGOS:** "do not chafe under her bonds"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't let her restraints chafe you"
**Issue:** Greek mē prosochthisēs = "do not be disgusted/wearied by." EMET "be weary" is closest to the Greek. Consensus: "do not be weary of her bonds."

---

## Disagreement 019 — v.28: "rest she gives" vs. "rest she offers"

**EMET:** "you will find the rest she gives"
**LOGOS:** "you will find the rest she offers"
**PNEUMA:** "what you find is rest"
**Issue:** Minor. Greek anapausis = "rest/repose." Consensus: EMET.

---

## Disagreement 020 — v.30: "blue thread" vs. "cord of blue"

**EMET:** "her bonds are a blue thread"
**LOGOS:** "her bonds are a cord of blue"
**PNEUMA:** "her cords shine blue and purple"
**Issue:** Greek desmoi autēs desmos hyakinthinon = "her bonds are a hyacinth cord." Hyacinth = purple-blue. PNEUMA adds "purple" (not in text). Consensus: "her bonds are a cord of blue."

---

## Disagreement 021 — v.31: "crown of gladness" vs. "crown of rejoicing" vs. "garland of celebration"

**EMET:** "put her on like a crown of gladness"
**LOGOS:** "put her on as a garland of celebration"
**PNEUMA:** "crown your head with her joy"
**Issue:** Greek stephanos agalliaseōs = "crown of exultation." "Gladness" (EMET) and "rejoicing" are both translations of agalliasis. Consensus: "a crown of rejoicing."

---

## Disagreement 022 — v.37: "give insight to your mind" vs. "instruct your mind"

**EMET:** "he will give insight to your mind"
**LOGOS:** "he himself will instruct your mind"
**PNEUMA:** "He himself will sharpen your mind"
**Issue:** Greek syniēsi kardian sou = "will give understanding to your heart." EMET "insight" is close. LOGOS "instruct" is weaker. PNEUMA "sharpen" is interpretive. Consensus: "he will give insight to your heart."

---
